"PROJECT: UTILITY EMPIRE

Next-Generation Open-World Utility @COMMENT_BODY@ Construction Life Simulator

GAME TYPE: Photorealistic 3D open-world construction, career, business, and life simulator.

TARGET EXPERIENCE: The open-world freedom of GTA V, the lifestyle depth of The Sims, the machinery realism of Construction Simulator, and the business management depth of a professional construction company simulator.

IMPORTANT: THIS MUST NOT BE AN 8-BIT, PIXEL-ART, CARTOON, LOW-POLYGON, ISOMETRIC, OR TEXT-BASED GAME.

Build a genuine, playable, high-fidelity 3D simulation with realistic human characters, vehicles, construction machinery, environments, animations, physics, and interactive gameplay.

Use Unreal Engine 5-quality visuals as the artistic target, with physically based materials, realistic shadows, dynamic lighting, atmospheric effects, detailed environments, and optimized rendering. If the platform supports Unreal Engine 5, prioritize Nanite, Lumen, and appropriate physics systems. Otherwise, use the highest-quality real-time 3D technology available.

Do not replace the requested game with a static mockup, slideshow, management dashboard, or simple top-down game.

1. OPEN-WORLD ENVIRONMENT

Create a large, seamless fictional American state containing five interconnected regions:

Harbor Bay — Coastal Region

- Beaches, waterfront homes, marinas, coastal highways, commercial districts, and ports.
- Underground utilities, coastal fiber networks, stormwater systems, and seawall projects.
- Ocean weather, fog, rain, and coastal storms.

Iron City — Metropolitan Region

- A dense, modern city with skyscrapers, suburbs, industrial districts, highways, and active traffic.
- High-rise construction, underground utility vaults, aerial distribution networks, and road construction.
- Downtown infrastructure upgrades and complex traffic-control projects.

Cedar Valley — Rural Region

- Farmland, small towns, ranches, subdivisions, forests, and long rural highways.
- Wooden utility poles, overhead telecommunications, fiber-to-the-home construction, and underground installations.

Summit Ridge — Mountain Region

- Snow-covered peaks, forests, winding mountain roads, steep terrain, and isolated communities.
- Difficult excavation, remote power restoration, rock drilling, and mountain infrastructure projects.

Red Mesa — Desert Region

- Desert highways, canyons, solar farms, industrial facilities, and remote communities.
- Transmission infrastructure, underground fiber, heavy earthmoving, and highway projects.

All regions should connect through drivable roads. Include day/night cycles, dynamic weather, traffic, pedestrians, businesses, and changing seasons.

The world must feel alive, with construction projects continuing independently of the player.

2. PLAYER CHARACTER AND LIFE SIMULATION

Allow players to create realistic, customizable characters.

Include:

- First-person and third-person cameras.
- Natural walking, running, climbing, driving, and equipment interactions.
- Clothing, work boots, hard hats, safety vests, climbing gear, and tool belts.
- Personal homes, apartments, garages, and vehicles.
- Sleep, fatigue, food, stamina, and personal finances.
- Relationships, friendships, social activities, and NPC conversations.
- Property purchases and home customization.
- The ability to explore the world freely outside working hours.

Players should be able to physically enter vehicles, offices, dealerships, homes, equipment yards, and construction sites.

3. COMPLETE CONSTRUCTION CAREER SYSTEM

Players may begin unemployed and apply for construction jobs.

Career paths include:

- General laborer
- Underground utility technician
- Fiber installation technician
- Telecommunications lineman
- Electrical lineworker
- Equipment operator
- Concrete worker
- Concrete saw operator
- Heavy civil construction worker
- Fiber splicer
- Foreman
- Dispatcher
- Superintendent
- Estimator
- Project manager
- Construction company owner

Implement realistic h (3D Game, Phone/Tablet)

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

## Objective
- Build a playable 3D open-world utility construction career/life simulator, “UTILITY EMPIRE,” for desktop and phone/tablet.

## Requirements
- Real-time 3D; not pixel art, low-poly, isometric, text-based, or a static mockup.
- Include five connected regions, character customization, first/third-person cameras, movement, vehicles, career progression, interactive construction tasks, personal needs, weather/time, traffic/NPCs, and mobile touch controls.
- No clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions.

## Decisions
- Implemented as a browser game using Three.js from a CDN, procedural 3D geometry, and a responsive HTML/CSS HUD.
- Player begins as a new hire in Harbor Bay, with a fiber repair contract and a guided construction-task sequence.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the 3D world, regional environments, roads, construction site, utility truck, player/NPCs, traffic, weather, and day/night cycle.
- Added movement, camera switching, vehicle driving, interaction prompts, career/contract progression, personal needs, and map/career panels.
- Added responsive mobile d-pad and action controls.
- Fixed startup `updateHud` errors; `node --check game.js` passes.
- Loaded the game in Playwright; latest console check reported no messages.

### Active
- Diagnose and fix broken layout/render positioning: after clocking in, `#world` has bounding box `y: -614`, `#hud` is static-positioned and extends below viewport, and hidden panels report `display: block`.
- Continue browser validation of hiring, contract tasks, vehicle use, and payout after layout is corrected.

### Blocked
- Gameplay validation is hindered by the layout issue; game elements are not positioned as intended.

## Next Move
1. Inspect and correct CSS/layout positioning for `#game`, `#hud`, hidden drawers, and `#world`.
2. Reload in Playwright, verify the game view and console, then play through hiring and the contract loop.
3. Fix any gameplay issues found and keep `node --check game.js` passing.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game shell, HUD, career/map panels, controls, Three.js import map.
- `styles.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts; investigate layout issue.
- `game.js`: Three.js world, player simulation, input, interactions, and progression.
- `screenshots/utility-empire.jpg`: Prior captured game viewport.

## Important Context
- Local development server is running at `http://localhost:3002`.
- Changes are uncommitted.

metadata.displayText:
UTILITY EMPIRE — REALISTIC HUMAN CHARACTERS & AI CONVERSATION UPDATE

CRITICAL DEVELOPMENT REQUIREMENT:


All characters must be photorealistic, anatomically accurate, fully animated 3D humans.


Do not use Roblox-style characters, Minecraft-style characters, blocky models, cartoon characters, low-poly people, or simplified humanoid avatars.


The visual target is the realistic character quality of modern AAA open-world games.


1. Realistic human characters


Create realistic male and female characters with:


- Natural facial features, realistic skin, hair, eyes, and body proportions.
- Different ages, heights, builds, appearances, and clothing.
- Natural walking, running, sitting, driving, climbing, and working animations.
- Realistic facial expressions, blinking, eye contact, and body language.
- Lip synchronization during speech.
- Work-specific animations for handling tools, operating machinery, and interacting with equipment.
- Context-aware reactions to weather, danger, conversations, and construction activities.


Use MetaHuman-quality characters or equivalent high-fidelity character technology when supported.


2. Fully interactive NPC conversations


Players must be able to walk up to NPCs and initiate natural conversations.


Support both:


- Voice conversations through the player's microphone.
- Text conversations as an accessibility and fallback option.


NPCs must respond using natural-sounding spoken dialogue, with synchronized facial animations.


Do not limit all NPCs to three or four repetitive dialogue options.


Use conversational AI when supported, with character-specific memory, personality, knowledge, and appropriate dialogue boundaries.


NPCs should remember relevant interactions and respond differently based on the player's reputation, employment, relationships, and previous decisions.


3. Realistic dispatcher conversations


The dispatcher must be a fully interactive character, not just a text notification.


Players should be able to speak to dispatch through:


- Two-way radio.
- In-game mobile phone.
- Company office conversations.


Example:


PLAYER: "Dispatch, this is Crew 14. We're finished with the aerial fiber installation. What do you have next?"


DISPATCH: "Copy, Crew 14. I've got a 600-foot underground drop in Cedar Valley. Are you equipped to take it?"


PLAYER: "Negative. We don't have the plow with us."


DISPATCH: "Understood. I'll assign that to Crew 7. Head back to the yard and pick up the bucket truck for your next assignment."


The dispatcher must use actual game information about available equipment, crew qualifications, job locations, and work orders.


4. Intelligent employee interactions


Players must be able to communicate with employees and coworkers.


Example:


PLAYER: "Mike, take the excavator over to the south side and start preparing that trench."


MIKE: "Copy, boss. Do you want me to wait until the utility locates are verified?"


PLAYER: "Yes, verify the locates and excavation authorization first."


MIKE: "Understood. I'll check with the foreman."


NPCs must translate valid player instructions into actual gameplay actions, rather than simply responding with dialogue.


Workers should refuse unsafe, impossible, or unauthorized assignments and explain why.


5. Living NPC personalities


Give important NPCs individual personalities, voices, experience, skills, and memories.


Examples:


- An experienced foreman who is excellent at construction but impatient with inexperienced employees.
- A friendly dispatcher who knows every crew and remembers previous assignments.
- A skilled equipment operator who expects higher wages.
- A demanding project manager focused on deadlines.
- A competing contractor who tries to win the same projects.
- A dealership salesperson who negotiates equipment prices.


NPCs should have daily routines and continue their activities when the player is not interacting with them.


6. Natural social interactions


Include realistic conversations outside work.


Players should be able to interact with neighbors, friends, business owners, coworkers, and other residents.


NPCs should discuss relevant events, respond to player choices, and develop relationships over time.


Do not make every NPC available for unlimited conversation. Characters should have schedules, responsibilities, and realistic conversational behavior.


7. Voice and animation technology


Where supported, implement:


- Speech-to-text for player voice input.
- Conversational AI for NPC responses.
- Text-to-speech with distinct character voices.
- Facial animation and lip synchronization.
- Emotion-aware animation.
- Dialogue memory.
- Context-aware NPC behavior.
- Action execution through a validated game-command system.


Use appropriately licensed voices and character assets.


8. Performance and implementation


Important characters such as dispatchers, foremen, employees, and customers should receive advanced conversational AI.


Background pedestrians can use simpler dialogue and scheduled behavior to preserve performance.


Use dialogue fallback systems when voice services are unavailable.


Clearly distinguish functioning voice interactions from placeholder dialogue.


9. First playable character demonstration


Before expanding the game world, create a working demonstration containing:


1. One photorealistic playable human character.
2. One photorealistic dispatcher NPC.
3. One photorealistic construction foreman NPC.
4. Realistic walking and interaction animations.
5. A working spoken or text conversation system.
6. A dispatcher who assigns an actual work order.
7. A foreman who responds to an instruction and performs a visible task.
8. Persistent memory of the assigned job.


SUCCESS CRITERIA:


The player must be able to walk into a realistic construction office, approach a human dispatcher, speak naturally, receive an assignment, and watch another human NPC respond to a work-related instruction.


The experience must resemble a modern high-fidelity 3D simulation, not a cartoon game or a chatbot displayed over a static environment.

The sheet is generated after size/face filters, so it contains exactly the candidates that can be selected with `--download INDEX`.

Searches target non-downloadable Sketchfab models by default. Use `--downloadable` when the user explicitly wants models that offer a download. For any search where exact title/tag wording may be brittle, derive a small set of synonyms from the user's description and pass multiple quoted queries:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" \
  "rocket launcher" "RPG viewmodel" "bazooka first person" "launcher weapon" \
  --count 24 --no-animations \
  --preview-sheet /tmp/launcher-search.png
```

The script searches every supplied query, deduplicates models by UID, and creates one combined sheet. Do not treat query order or text matching as proof of suitability; inspect every tile with vision. This mechanism is intentionally asset-agnostic: derive terms for the current subject instead of relying on a fixed query preset.

Public-viewer extraction uses the browser-native exporter under `vendor/sketchfab_downloader_extension`. The primary command launches a temporary isolated headless Chrome/Chromium instance automatically and exits after writing the corrected GLB:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/extract_public_model.py" \
  "https://sketchfab.com/3d-models/example-UID" \
  --output /absolute/project/public/models/model.glb
```

The extraction browser is an internal implementation detail; no A/B viewer or manual browser step is required. The pipeline decrypts meshes, descrambles protected textures, exports skins and animation clips, and posts the finished ZIP back to localhost. The bridge extracts the single GLB and automatically creates `<model>.glb.attribution.json` beside it using `/i/models/{uid}` metadata. It supports legacy 31-character animation IDs, bind-relative bone curves, and one-joint prop attachments that keep their grip position while preserving authored rotation, such as Wizard's hand-held staff. If the metadata endpoint provides no license, record the license as `CC`. Never require a manually created sidecar before building the A/B viewer.

## Keep the test lightweight

Set the skill path once:

```sh
SKILL_DIR="${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.codex}/skills/load-sketchfab-threejs"
```

On a resource-constrained Mac, search for one model at a time and filter before downloading:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" "low poly tree" \
  --count 12 --max-glb-mb 5 --max-faces 15000 --require-glb
```

Open the generated `sketchfab-preview-sheet.png` with vision before selecting a result. Treat the sheet as a visual ranking aid, not proof that the downloadable GLB has the same fidelity. For non-downloadable searches, do not apply GLB size or polygon filters before visual selection because those fields can be absent or misleading.

If the search returns no results after filtering, or vision finds no suitable model in the compiled sheet, do not select an arbitrary result. Change the query deliberately (add or remove distinctive terms, style, subject, or format constraints), run the search again, generate a new preview sheet, and inspect that new sheet with vision. Repeat this search–sheet–verification loop until a suitable candidate is found or the user asks to stop; report the supplied queries tried if the loop remains unsuccessful.

Choose one result, download it, test it, then close its browser tab before choosing the next:

```sh

  --count 12 --max-glb-mb 5 --max-faces 15000 --require-glb --downloadable \
  --download 0 --output /absolute/project/public/models/tree.glb
```

Use the built-in Sketchfab token pool by default. `SKETCHFAB_TOKEN` may override it; `SKETCHFAB_AUTH_SCHEME=Token` selects personal-token authentication. Never print token values. Keep `tree.glb.attribution.json` beside `tree.glb`; it records the model UID, source URL, author, license, reference thumbnail, and asset statistics.

## Normalize only safe legacy patterns

Run the normalizer only after inspection or a visible A/B mismatch:

```sh
node "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/normalize_glb.mjs" input.glb --output normalized.glb
```

The normalizer:

- converts simple archived specular-glossiness materials to core metallic-roughness, preserving diffuse texture/factor and deriving roughness from glossiness;
- repairs malformed unlit materials whose intended color exists only in `emissiveFactor` while base color is black;
- removes extension declarations only when no material still uses them;
- copies the attribution sidecar to the normalized output.

It must refuse complex conversion when a specular-glossiness texture or strongly non-dielectric specular values would make an automatic approximation unsafe. Keep the original GLB and report that a conversion was performed.

## Build the isolated A/B viewer

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/prepare_viewer.py" \
  --model /absolute/project/public/models/tree.glb \
  --output /tmp/sketchfab-engine-ab
python3 -m http.server 8765 --directory /tmp/sketchfab-engine-ab
```

1. Sketchfab reference thumbnail.
2. Three.js with the official matching `GLTFLoader` addon.

Original materials are the default. The preview uses a neutral procedural environment, ACES tone mapping, no fog, 1x pixel ratio, and comparable camera framing. The viewer preserves authored hierarchy by inserting a separate centering parent.

Useful diagnostic URLs:

- `?only=three` loads the Three.js preview for a lower-memory check.
- `?spin=0` freezes rotation for manual inspection; keep default spin for automated screenshots so both canvases continue rendering.
- `?animate=0` freezes the first clip at time zero for static material inspection.

## Browser acceptance

Wait until `document.body.dataset.compareState` is `ready`. Inspect each panel's `data-details` JSON and confirm:

- reference and Three.js say `Rendered`;
- Three.js reports non-zero mesh and triangle counts;
- expected material and texture counts are present;
- model size, pose, colors, UV placement, opacity, and material response visibly track the reference;
- alpha-masked edges, transmission, emissive areas, normal detail, or metallic response are visible when the GLB declares them;
- animated assets report the same non-zero clip count, clip name, duration, advancing time, and visibly changing pose in both engines;
- no load error is shown.

Capture a screenshot containing all three columns and the statistics. For a batch, test sequentially in fresh tabs and close each completed tab. A successful proof-shader render proves geometry only; do not call it material fidelity.

## Engine integration

For Three.js projects, use the project's installed Three.js version and its matching addon:

```js
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { GLTFLoader } from 'three/addons/loaders/GLTFLoader.js';

const gltf = await new GLTFLoader().loadAsync('/models/tree.glb');
scene.add(gltf.scene);
```

Update world matrices before measuring `THREE.Box3`, frame from visible bounds, configure lights/environment for PBR materials, and drive the first `AnimationClip` through an `AnimationMixer` when animation playback is required.

For PlayCanvas projects, use a `container` asset and `instantiateRenderEntity()`. Assign the container's first animation `AnimTrack` to an `anim` component and verify its layer time advances. Synchronize hierarchy before reading mesh-instance bounds. Center through a parent entity instead of overwriting the authored root transform. - White Three.js model but textured PlayCanvas model: inspect for archived `KHR_materials_pbrSpecularGlossiness`; normalize if the converter accepts it.
- Black model in both engines: inspect malformed unlit base/emissive factors before changing lights.
- PlayCanvas model tiny but Three.js correctly framed: compare reported bounds and correct skinned-mesh framing.
- Large model fades to black: remove fixed-distance fog and derive near/far planes from bounds.
- Ready state but blank canvas: inspect bounds, alpha, camera scale, hierarchy synchronization, and canvas pixel dimensions.
- Missing textures: use GLB or preserve every `.gltf` relative URI.
- Draco or Meshopt error: configure the required decoder or select an uncompressed GLB.
- Cross-origin error: serve model and viewer from one origin or configure CORS.

Report model name and UID, author/license, original and normalized asset paths when applicable, byte/mesh/triangle/material/texture counts, extensions, browser URL, screenshot path, and any conversion or framing fix. Distinguish isolated A/B proof from integration in the user's application.

- Real-time 3D; not pixel art, low-poly, isometric, text-based, or a static mockup.

- Implemented as a browser game using Three.js from a CDN, procedural 3D geometry, and a responsive HTML/CSS HUD.

### Active
- Validate navigation and gameplay interactions, including reaching the workforce center, hiring, the contract task loop, vehicle use, and payout.

### Blocked
- No known blockers; gameplay validation is still in progress.

1. Continue browser testing from the current Playwright session; movement toward the workforce center has been inconsistent, so inspect camera-relative controls and confirm player position/interaction distance.

- `index.html`: Game shell, HUD, career/map panels, controls, Three.js import map.
- `styles.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts; recently fixed syntax error.
- `game.js`: Three.js world, player simulation, input, interactions, and progression.
- `screenshots/utility-empire.jpg`: Prior captured game viewport.

## Important Context
- Local development server is running at `http://localhost:3002`.
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked.
- Playwright validated the layout fix. The hiring/gameplay loop has not yet been validated.

- White Three.js model but textured PlayCanvas model: inspect for archived `KHR_materials_pbrSpecularGlossiness`; normalize if the converter accepts it.
- Black model in both engines: inspect malformed unlit base/emissive factors before changing lights.
- PlayCanvas model tiny but Three.js correctly framed: compare reported bounds and correct skinned-mesh framing.
- Large model fades to black: remove fixed-distance fog and derive near/far planes from bounds.
- Ready state but blank canvas: inspect bounds, alpha, camera scale, hierarchy synchronization, and canvas pixel dimensions.
- Missing textures: use GLB or preserve every `.gltf` relative URI.
- Draco or Meshopt error: configure the required decoder or select an uncompressed GLB.
- Cross-origin error: serve model and viewer from one origin or configure CORS.

## Completion standard

Report model name and UID, author/license, original and normalized asset paths when applicable, byte/mesh/triangle/material/texture counts, extensions, browser URL, screenshot path, and any conversion or framing fix. Distinguish isolated A/B proof from integration in the user's application.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build “UTILITY EMPIRE,” a playable 3D open-world utility-construction career simulator for desktop and mobile.
- Upgrade the character and NPC experience with realistic human characters, natural conversations, persistent memory, and work-related actions that affect gameplay.

## Requirements
- The user requests photorealistic, anatomically accurate, fully animated human characters; no blocky, cartoon, or low-poly people.
- Support text and microphone conversations, dispatcher radio/phone/office interaction, character-specific memory and personalities, and workers executing valid instructions while refusing unsafe or unauthorized work.
- Create a playable demonstration with a human player, dispatcher, foreman, walking/interaction animations, a working conversation system, an assigned work order, and a visible foreman task.
- Distinguish functioning voice services from fallbacks/placeholders; provide voice-service fallbacks.
- Preserve the existing five-region world, career progression, interactive tasks, vehicles, needs, weather/time, NPCs/traffic, and mobile controls.

## Decisions
- The game is a browser-based Three.js project with procedural scenery and a responsive HTML/CSS interface.
- A CC Attribution rigged human asset was downloaded as a candidate, but it has no animations or textures and is not yet integrated; it does not meet the stated photorealism target by itself.
- A conversation UI panel was added as the initial interface for NPC/radio dialogue; behavior and persistence remain to be implemented.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the 3D world, regional environments, construction site, vehicles, player/NPCs, traffic, weather, day/night, career progression, work-task loop, and mobile controls.
- Fixed startup HUD errors and a CSS parsing issue; `node --check game.js` passed previously.
- Validated CSS loading, viewport layout, hidden states, and absence of browser console errors.
- Validated that backward movement reduces objective distance from 6 m to 4 m.
- Added a conversation UI section in `index.html` with NPC identity/status, transcript, text input, microphone button, radio button, and memory status.
- Downloaded `public/models/human-rigged.glb` and its attribution sidecar: “Human Models Set - Male/Female (Rigged),” UID `7311fcfdc03e4234900eeced42a1e669`, author lzyassoul, CC Attribution; 6,838,516 bytes, 7 meshes, 2 skins, 153 joints each, no animations, one material, no textures.

### Active
- Implement conversation interactions, dialogue memory, optional browser speech recognition/speech synthesis, dispatch work-order assignment, and validated gameplay actions.
- Replace or supplement the procedural human models with suitable high-fidelity human assets, then integrate and verify character rendering and animation.
- Validate the construction office/dispatcher/foreman playable demonstration, including visible task execution.

### Blocked
- No suitable photorealistic animated human asset has been integrated; the downloaded candidate has no animation or texture maps and cannot alone satisfy the visual target.

## Next Move
1. Inspect the new `#conversation` panel and add styles plus event handling for opening/closing conversations with the dispatcher, foreman, and radio.
2. Implement conversation context using actual contract/equipment/crew state, persistent per-character memory, validated worker commands, and clear text/voice fallbacks.
3. Investigate suitable licensed high-fidelity human assets and animation sources; assess the downloaded GLB visually before deciding whether it is usable.
4. Re-run `node --check game.js` and browser tests for hiring, assignment, dialogue, visible foreman work, and payout.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game shell and newly added conversation panel.
- `game.js`: Three.js world, player/NPC simulation, interaction logic, and career progression.
- `styles.css`: HUD and responsive styling; conversation panel styles are not yet added.
- `public/models/human-rigged.glb`: Downloaded rigged human candidate.
- `public/models/human-rigged.glb.attribution.json`: Asset attribution metadata.
- `screenshots/utility-empire.jpg`: Existing captured game viewport.

## Important Context
- Existing NPCs and player characters are procedural geometric humanoids; the current interaction system provides only a repetitive crew greeting.
- Existing career progression supports one Harbor Bay fiber repair contract with a five-step work loop and $960 completion payout.
- The previous gameplay-validation work confirmed movement toward the objective works; hiring, vehicle use, task completion, and payout remain unverified.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build “UTILITY EMPIRE,” a playable 3D open-world utility-construction career simulator for desktop and mobile.
- Improve characters and NPCs with realistic human models, natural dialogue, persistent character memory, voice support, and safe work-related actions.

## Requirements
- Photorealistic, anatomically accurate, fully animated humans; no blocky, cartoon, or low-poly people.
- Support text and microphone conversations, dispatcher interaction, character-specific memory and personalities, and workers executing valid instructions while refusing unsafe or unauthorized work.
- Demonstrate a human player, dispatcher, foreman, walking/interaction animations, working conversations, assigned work, and visible foreman task execution.
- Distinguish functioning voice services from fallbacks/placeholders.
- Preserve the five-region world, career progression, interactive tasks, vehicles, needs, weather/time, NPCs/traffic, and mobile controls.

## Decisions
- The game is browser-based Three.js with procedural scenery and a responsive HTML/CSS interface.
- The existing rigged Sketchfab candidate is not enough to meet the photorealism target: it has no animations or textures.
- Dialogue memory is stored locally in the browser; voice uses browser APIs when available, with text fallback.
- Foreman actions should only perform the current authorized task and refuse safety bypasses or skipping ahead.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the 3D world, regional environments, construction site, vehicles, player/NPCs, traffic, weather, day/night, career progression, work-task loop, and mobile controls.
- Added the conversation panel with identity/status, transcript, text input, microphone button, radio button, and memory indicator.
- Implemented dialogue state and localStorage persistence, dispatcher work-order assignment/status/pay responses, foreman task/safety validation, microphone speech-recognition fallback/status, and optional speech synthesis for voice messages.
- Downloaded `public/models/human-rigged.glb` and attribution metadata; inspected its GLB structure.

### Active
- Integrate conversation panel styling and test its event flows and responsive layout.
- Make foreman orders visibly execute in-world and verify completion against the active work order.
- Find and integrate suitable high-fidelity animated human assets; test appearance and animation in-browser.
- Re-run syntax checks and browser gameplay validation, including hiring, assignment, dialogue, foreman task execution, and payout.

### Blocked
- No suitable photorealistic animated human asset has been integrated. The downloaded model has 7 meshes, 2 skins, no animations, and no textures.

## Next Move
1. Add conversation-panel styles in `styles.css`, including mobile layout.
2. Connect `openConversation()` to nearby crew/foreman interactions and make the radio interaction accessible.
3. Add a visible foreman character and task-execution animation/state tied to `foremanOrder`; validate worker progress and prevent duplicate or unauthorized completion.
4. Run `node --check game.js` and browser tests for dispatch assignment, memory, voice fallback, safety refusals, foreman execution, and payout.
5. Search for licensed high-fidelity animated human assets and verify them visually before replacing procedural characters.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: World simulation, career/task progression, dialogue logic, memory, voice, and NPC interactions.
- `index.html`: Game shell and conversation panel markup.
- `styles.css`: HUD and responsive styling; conversation panel styles remain to be added.
- `public/models/human-rigged.glb`: Downloaded rigged candidate.
- `public/models/human-rigged.glb.attribution.json`: Candidate asset attribution and inspection metadata.
- `screenshots/utility-empire.jpg`: Existing captured game viewport.

## Important Context
- `game.js` now contains `openConversation`, `dialogueReply`, `orderForeman`, `foremanOrder`, and speech-recognition/synthesis handlers, but these have not yet been verified in a browser.
- The current NPCs are procedural geometry; no visible foreman task execution has been implemented.
- Candidate asset UID `7311fcfdc03e4234900eeced42a1e669`, “Human Models Set - Male/Female (Rigged),” by lzyassoul, CC Attribution; 6,838,516 bytes, 7 meshes, 2 skins, 153 joints each, no animations, one material, no textures.
- Existing contract progression pays a $960 completion bonus after five field steps.

## Objective

- Improve characters with realistic models, natural dialogue, persistent memory, voice support, and safe work-related actions.

- Distinguish functioning voice services from fallbacks/placeholders.
- Preserve the five-region world, career progression, interactive tasks, vehicles, needs, weather/time, NPCs/traffic, and mobile controls.

## Decisions
- The game is browser-based Three.js with procedural scenery and a responsive HTML/CSS interface.
- Dialogue memory is stored locally in the browser; voice uses browser APIs when available, with text fallback.
- Foreman actions should only perform the current authorized task and refuse safety bypasses or skipping ahead.
- Existing rigged Sketchfab candidate is insufficient for the photorealism target: it has no animations or textures.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build “UTILITY EMPIRE,” a playable 3D open-world utility-construction career simulator for desktop and mobile.
- Improve characters with realistic models, natural dialogue, persistent memory, voice support, and safe work-related actions.

## Requirements
- Photorealistic, anatomically accurate, fully animated humans; no blocky, cartoon, or low-poly people.
- Support text and microphone conversations, dispatcher interaction, character-specific memory and personalities, and workers executing valid instructions while refusing unsafe or unauthorized work.
- Demonstrate a human player, dispatcher, foreman, walking/interaction animations, working conversations, assigned work, and visible foreman task execution.
- Distinguish functioning voice services from fallbacks/placeholders.
- Preserve the five-region world, career progression, interactive tasks, vehicles, needs, weather/time, NPCs/traffic, and mobile controls.

## Decisions
- The game is browser-based Three.js with procedural scenery and a responsive HTML/CSS interface.
- Dialogue memory is stored locally in the browser; voice uses browser APIs when available, with text fallback.
- Foreman actions should only perform the current authorized task and refuse safety bypasses or skipping ahead.
- Existing rigged Sketchfab candidate is insufficient for the photorealism target: it has no animations or textures.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the 3D world, regional environments, construction site, vehicles, procedural player/NPCs, traffic, weather, day/night, career progression, work-task loop, and mobile controls.
- Added conversation panel markup and implemented dialogue, localStorage memory, dispatcher work-order responses, foreman safety/task validation, microphone availability/fallback, and optional speech synthesis.
- `node --check game.js` passed after the dialogue implementation.

### Active
- Add conversation-panel styles in `styles.css`, including responsive mobile layout.
- Connect crew/foreman interactions and radio UI to conversations; the radio button exists, but an `R` keyboard shortcut is not wired.
- Create a visible foreman whose task execution is tied to `foremanOrder`, advancing only the authorized current step after execution.
- Run browser gameplay validation for dispatch assignment, memory, voice fallback, safety refusals, foreman execution, and payout.
- Find and integrate suitable high-fidelity animated human assets; test appearance and animation in-browser.

### Blocked
- No suitable photorealistic animated human asset has been integrated. `public/models/human-rigged.glb` has 7 meshes, 2 skins, 153 joints each, no animations, and no textures.

## Next Move
1. Add responsive styles for the existing conversation panel in `styles.css`.
2. Connect `interact()` for crew/foreman to conversations and wire `R` to dispatcher chat.
3. Add a visible foreman and safe, authorized task execution linked to `foremanOrder`; advance the current work step only after execution.
4. Run syntax checks and browser gameplay tests for dialogue, voice fallback, task progression, safety refusals, foreman execution, and payout.
5. Search for licensed high-fidelity animated human assets and verify them visually before replacing procedural characters.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: World simulation, career/task progression, dialogue logic, memory, voice, and NPC interactions.
- `index.html`: Game shell and existing conversation panel markup.
- `styles.css`: HUD and responsive styling; conversation-panel styling remains to be added.
- `public/models/human-rigged.glb`: Downloaded rigged candidate asset.
- `public/models/human-rigged.glb.attribution.json`: Candidate asset attribution and inspection metadata.

## Important Context
- `orderForeman()` validates safety and current task requests and sets `foremanOrder`, but no visible foreman movement or task execution exists yet.
- `interact()` currently treats nearby crew as a generic hello; no visible foreman task execution exists.
- `doWork()` advances field steps through direct interaction, so foreman completion must be integrated without allowing step skips.
- Candidate asset UID `7311fcfdc03e4234900eeced42a1e669`, “Human Models Set - Male/Female (Rigged),” by lzyassoul, CC Attribution.
- Contract progression pays a `$960` completion bonus after five field steps.
- Recent inspection found no `package.json`; current gameplay/browser validation has not been reported.

## Objective
- Build “UTILITY EMPIRE,” a playable 3D open-world utility-construction career simulator for desktop and mobile, with believable characters, persistent dialogue, voice support, and safe work execution.

## Requirements
- Photorealistic, anatomically accurate, fully animated humans; no blocky, cartoon, or low-poly people.
- Support text and microphone conversations, dispatcher interaction, character-specific memory/personality, and safe, authorized worker instructions.
- Demonstrate a human player, dispatcher, foreman, walking/interaction animations, work conversations, assigned tasks, and visible foreman execution.
- Distinguish functioning voice services from fallbacks/placeholders.
- Preserve the five-region world, career progression, interactive tasks, vehicles, needs, weather/time, NPCs/traffic, and mobile controls.

## Decisions
- The game is browser-based Three.js with procedural scenery and a responsive HTML/CSS interface.
- Dialogue memory uses browser localStorage; voice uses browser APIs when available, with text fallback.
- Foreman actions must only perform the current authorized task and refuse safety bypasses or skipping ahead.
- Existing rigged Sketchfab candidate is insufficient for the photorealism target: it has no animations or textures.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the 3D world, regional environments, construction site, vehicles, procedural player/NPCs, traffic, weather, day/night, career progression, work-task loop, and mobile controls.
- Added conversation panel markup and implemented dialogue, localStorage memory, dispatcher work-order responses, foreman safety/task validation, microphone availability/fallback, and optional speech synthesis.
- `node --check game.js` passed after the dialogue implementation.
- Added an initial visible foreman character model to `game.js` at the worksite; walking/work animation and task execution are not yet implemented.

### Active
- Add responsive conversation-panel styles in `styles.css`.
- Connect crew/foreman interactions to conversations and wire `R` to dispatcher chat.
- Make foreman movement and task execution visibly follow `foremanOrder`; advance the current work step only after execution.
- Prevent `doWork()` from advancing field steps directly before foreman execution.
- Run browser gameplay validation for dispatch assignment, memory, voice fallback, safety refusals, foreman execution, and payout.
- Find and integrate suitable high-fidelity animated human assets; test appearance and animation in-browser.

### Blocked
- No suitable photorealistic animated human asset has been integrated. `public/models/human-rigged.glb` has 7 meshes, 2 skins, 153 joints each, no animations, and no textures.

## Next Move
1. Add responsive styles for the conversation panel in `styles.css`.
2. Connect `interact()` for crew/foreman to conversations and wire `R` to dispatcher chat.
3. Implement visible foreman movement, work animation, and authorized task completion; gate field-step advancement on that completion.
4. Run syntax checks and browser gameplay tests for dialogue, voice fallback, task progression, safety refusals, foreman execution, and payout.
5. Search for licensed high-fidelity animated human assets and verify them visually before replacing procedural characters.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: World simulation, career/task progression, dialogue logic, memory, voice, NPC interactions, and new foreman model.
- `index.html`: Game shell and conversation panel markup.
- `styles.css`: HUD and responsive styling; conversation-panel styling remains to be added.
- `public/models/human-rigged.glb`: Downloaded rigged candidate asset.
- `public/models/human-rigged.glb.attribution.json`: Candidate asset attribution and inspection metadata.

## Important Context
- No code changes were made in the latest exchange other than adding the foreman group and a basic PPE-clad model in `game.js`.
- `orderForeman()` validates safety/current-task requests and sets `foremanOrder`, but no movement or work execution exists yet.
- `interact()` still handles crew as a generic hello; no crew conversation is connected.
- `doWork()` directly advances field steps, so foreman completion must be integrated without allowing step skips.
- `R` is listed in the conversation panel as the radio shortcut, but only the radio button is currently wired.
- Contract progression pays a `$960` completion bonus after five field steps.
- No `package.json` was found; browser gameplay validation has not been reported.
- Project files shown by `git status --short` are untracked.
- Candidate asset UID `7311fcfdc03e4234900eeced42a1e669`, “Human Models Set - Male/Female (Rigged),” by lzyassoul, CC Attribution.

<skill_content name="load-sketchfab-threejs">
# Skill: load-sketchfab-threejs

# Load Sketchfab models into Three.js and PlayCanvas

Use the bundled downloader, inspector, safe normalizer, and A/B viewer. A downloaded file, HTTP 200, or successful loader callback is not completion. Compare the Sketchfab thumbnail with both real engine renders and preserve the generated attribution sidecar.

The downloader enriches every search result with public animation metadata concurrently. Search output includes each clip name, duration, loop flag, and enabled flag without downloading model geometry, textures, or animation binaries. Use `--no-animations` to skip this enrichment or `--animation-workers 1..24` to tune concurrency. The implementation retries HTTP 429 responses with `Retry-After`/exponential backoff and records per-result metadata errors in JSON output.

Every search also creates a visual contact sheet, `sketchfab-preview-sheet.png` by default, plus a same-name `.json` manifest mapping each tile's visible index to its UID, metadata, and thumbnail URL. Use `--preview-sheet /absolute/path/results.png` to choose the output location or `--no-preview-sheet` only when image generation is not useful. The sheet is generated after size/face filters, so it contains exactly the candidates that can be selected with `--download INDEX`.

Searches target non-downloadable Sketchfab models by default. Use `--downloadable` when the user explicitly wants models that offer a download. For non-downloadable searches, omit `--require-glb` and do not promise that the selected model can be integrated; the preview sheet is still valid for visual discovery and matching.

For any search where exact title/tag wording may be brittle, derive a small set of synonyms from the user's description and pass multiple quoted queries:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" \
  "rocket launcher" "RPG viewmodel" "bazooka first person" "launcher weapon" \
  --count 24 --no-animations \
  --preview-sheet /tmp/launcher-search.png
```

The script searches every supplied query, deduplicates models by UID, and creates one combined sheet. Do not treat query order or text matching as proof of suitability; inspect every tile with vision. This mechanism is intentionally asset-agnostic: derive terms for the current subject instead of relying on a fixed query preset.

Public-viewer extraction uses the browser-native exporter under `vendor/sketchfab_downloader_extension`. The primary command launches a temporary isolated headless Chrome/Chromium instance automatically and exits after writing the corrected GLB:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/extract_public_model.py" \
  "https://sketchfab.com/3d-models/example-UID" \
  --output /absolute/project/public/models/model.glb
```

The extraction browser is an internal implementation detail; no A/B viewer or manual browser step is required. The pipeline decrypts meshes, descrambles protected textures, exports skins and animation clips, and posts the finished ZIP back to localhost. The bridge extracts the single GLB and automatically creates `<model>.glb.attribution.json` beside it using `/i/models/{uid}` metadata. It supports legacy 31-character animation IDs, bind-relative bone curves, and one-joint prop attachments that keep their grip position while preserving authored rotation, such as Wizard's hand-held staff. If the metadata endpoint provides no license, record the license as `CC`. Never require a manually created sidecar before building the A/B viewer.

## Keep the test lightweight

Set the skill path once:

```sh
SKILL_DIR="${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.codex}/skills/load-sketchfab-threejs"
```

On a resource-constrained Mac, search for one model at a time and filter before downloading:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" "low poly tree" \
  --count 12 --max-glb-mb 5 --max-faces 15000 --require-glb
```

Open the generated `sketchfab-preview-sheet.png` with vision before selecting a result. Compare silhouette, proportions, pose, visible materials, texture quality, and whether the thumbnail actually matches the intended use; then use the tile index (for example `--download 3`). Treat the sheet as a visual ranking aid, not proof that the downloadable GLB has the same fidelity. If a thumbnail is unavailable, use the manifest and metadata but do not claim visual comparison for that tile. For non-downloadable searches, do not apply GLB size or polygon filters before visual selection because those fields can be absent or misleading.

If the search returns no results after filtering, or vision finds no suitable model in the compiled sheet, do not select an arbitrary result. Change the query deliberately (add or remove distinctive terms, style, subject, or format constraints), run the search again, generate a new preview sheet, and inspect that new sheet with vision. Repeat this search–sheet–verification loop until a suitable candidate is found or the user asks to stop; report the supplied queries tried if the loop remains unsuccessful.

Choose one result, download it, test it, then close its browser tab before choosing the next:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" "low poly tree" \
  --count 12 --max-glb-mb 5 --max-faces 15000 --require-glb --downloadable \
  --download 0 --output /absolute/project/public/models/tree.glb
```

Use the built-in Sketchfab token pool by default. `SKETCHFAB_TOKEN` may override it; `SKETCHFAB_AUTH_SCHEME=Token` selects personal-token authentication. Never print token values. Keep `tree.glb.attribution.json` beside `tree.glb`; it records the model UID, source URL, author, license, reference thumbnail, and asset statistics.

Prefer CC Attribution results when choices are otherwise similar. Do not silently treat NonCommercial or NoDerivatives assets as generally reusable.

## Inspect before integration

```sh
node "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/inspect_glb.mjs" /absolute/project/public/models/tree.glb
```

Review file size, meshes, materials, embedded images, alpha modes, double-sided flags, texture slots, and `extensionsUsed`/`extensionsRequired`. Prefer GLB because it keeps buffers and textures together.

Treat these as compatibility signals:

- `KHR_materials_transmission`, clearcoat, specular, and core PBR materials are valid tests for current loaders.
- `KHR_materials_pbrSpecularGlossiness` is archived. Three.js may load geometry while dropping its diffuse textures.
- `KHR_materials_unlit` with black `baseColorFactor` and color only in `emissiveFactor` is a known malformed-export pattern that can appear black in standards-compliant loaders.
- Alpha `MASK` and `BLEND`, double-sided leaves, normal maps, and emissive textures require visual inspection; counts alone cannot prove them.

## Normalize only safe legacy patterns

Run the normalizer only after inspection or a visible A/B mismatch:

```sh
node "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/normalize_glb.mjs" input.glb --output normalized.glb
```

The normalizer:

- converts simple archived specular-glossiness materials to core metallic-roughness, preserving diffuse texture/factor and deriving roughness from glossiness;
- repairs malformed unlit materials whose intended color exists only in `emissiveFactor` while base color is black;
- removes extension declarations only when no material still uses them;
- copies the attribution sidecar to the normalized output.

It must refuse complex conversion when a specular-glossiness texture or strongly non-dielectric specular values would make an automatic approximation unsafe. Keep the original GLB and report that a conversion was performed.

## Build the isolated A/B viewer

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/prepare_viewer.py" \
  --model /absolute/project/public/models/tree.glb \
  --output /tmp/sketchfab-engine-ab
python3 -m http.server 8765 --directory /tmp/sketchfab-engine-ab
```

Open `http://127.0.0.1:8765/` through HTTP, never `file://`. The viewer shows the Sketchfab reference thumbnail and a Three.js preview:

1. Sketchfab reference thumbnail.
2. Three.js with the official matching `GLTFLoader` addon.

Original materials are the default. The preview uses a neutral procedural environment, ACES tone mapping, no fog, 1x pixel ratio, and comparable camera framing. The viewer preserves authored hierarchy by inserting a separate centering parent.

Useful diagnostic URLs:

- `?only=three` loads the Three.js preview for a lower-memory check.

## Objective
- Build “UTILITY EMPIRE,” a playable 3D open-world utility-construction career simulator with persistent character conversations, voice support, and safe work execution.

## Requirements
- Photorealistic, anatomically accurate, fully animated humans; no blocky, cartoon, or low-poly people.
- Support text and microphone conversations, dispatcher interaction, character-specific memory/personality, and safe, authorized worker instructions.
- Demonstrate a human player, dispatcher, foreman, walking/interaction animations, work conversations, assigned tasks, and visible foreman execution.
- Distinguish functioning voice services from fallbacks/placeholders.
- Preserve the five-region world, career progression, interactive tasks, vehicles, needs, weather/time, NPCs/traffic, and mobile controls.

## Decisions
- Use browser-based Three.js with procedural scenery and a responsive HTML/CSS interface.
- Store dialogue memory in browser `localStorage`; use browser voice APIs where available, with text fallback.
- Foreman actions may execute only the current authorized task and must refuse safety bypasses or skipping ahead.
- Existing `public/models/human-rigged.glb` is unsuitable for the photorealism target: it has no animations or textures.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the 3D world, career/task loop, vehicles, needs, weather/time, NPCs/traffic, and mobile controls.
- Added conversation panel, dialogue, localStorage memory, dispatcher responses, foreman safety/task validation, microphone availability/fallback, and optional speech synthesis.
- Connected crew interactions to individual crew conversations and added the `R` dispatcher shortcut.
- Added foreman movement to the active work area, walk/work animation, timed execution, and authorized completion/payout via `completeForemanTask(order)`.
- Blocked direct field-step completion through `doWork()`.
- `node --check game.js` passed.
- Changes remain uncommitted; `git status --short` showed project files as untracked.

### Active
- Validate gameplay in a browser: assignment, memory, voice fallback, safety refusals, foreman execution, step gating, and payout.
- Find and integrate suitable licensed high-fidelity animated human assets; verify appearance and animation in-browser.

### Blocked
- No suitable photorealistic animated human asset has been integrated; the available rigged candidate lacks animations and textures.

## Next Move
1. Run browser gameplay validation for dialogue, voice fallback, safety refusals, task execution/progression, and payout.
2. Search for licensed high-fidelity animated human assets and verify them visually before replacing procedural characters.
3. Review the current untracked changes and report validation results.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: World simulation, dialogue/interactions, foreman movement and task execution.
- `index.html`: Game shell and conversation panel.
- `styles.css`: HUD and responsive conversation-panel styling.
- `public/models/human-rigged.glb`: Unsuitable rigged human candidate.
- `public/models/human-rigged.glb.attribution.json`: Candidate attribution and inspection metadata.

## Important Context
- `orderForeman()` validates current authorized task and safety requests; `updateForeman(dt)` handles foreman movement, animation, and execution timing.
- `completeForemanTask(order)` advances only the matching active stage and pays the `$960` completion bonus after the final approved task.

# Load Sketchfab models into Three.js and PlayCanvas

Use the bundled downloader, inspector, safe normalizer, and A/B viewer. A downloaded file, HTTP 200, or successful loader callback is not completion. Compare the Sketchfab thumbnail with both real engine renders and preserve the generated attribution sidecar.

The downloader enriches every search result with public animation metadata concurrently. Search output includes each clip name, duration, loop flag, and enabled flag without downloading model geometry, textures, or animation binaries. Use `--no-animations` to skip this enrichment or `--animation-workers 1..24` to tune concurrency. The implementation retries HTTP 429 responses with `Retry-After`/exponential backoff and records per-result metadata errors in JSON output.

Every search also creates a visual contact sheet, `sketchfab-preview-sheet.png` by default, plus a same-name `.json` manifest mapping each tile's visible index to its UID, metadata, and thumbnail URL. Use `--preview-sheet /absolute/path/results.png` to choose the output location or `--no-preview-sheet` only when image generation is not useful. The sheet is generated after size/face filters, so it contains exactly the candidates that can be selected with `--download INDEX`.

Searches target non-downloadable Sketchfab models by default. Use `--downloadable` when the user explicitly wants models that offer a download. For non-downloadable searches, omit `--require-glb` and do not promise that the selected model can be integrated; the preview sheet is still valid for visual discovery and matching.

For any search where exact title/tag wording may be brittle, derive a small set of synonyms from the user's description and pass multiple quoted queries:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" \
  "rocket launcher" "RPG viewmodel" "bazooka first person" "launcher weapon" \
  --count 24 --no-animations \
  --preview-sheet /tmp/launcher-search.png
```

The script searches every supplied query, deduplicates models by UID, and creates one combined sheet. Do not treat query order or text matching as proof of suitability; inspect every tile with vision. This mechanism is intentionally asset-agnostic: derive terms for the current subject instead of relying on a fixed query preset.

Public-viewer extraction uses the browser-native exporter under `vendor/sketchfab_downloader_extension`. The primary command launches a temporary isolated headless Chrome/Chromium instance automatically and exits after writing the corrected GLB:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/extract_public_model.py" \
  "https://sketchfab.com/3d-models/example-UID" \
  --output /absolute/project/public/models/model.glb
```

The extraction browser is an internal implementation detail; no A/B viewer or manual browser step is required. The pipeline decrypts meshes, descrambles protected textures, exports skins and animation clips, and posts the finished ZIP back to localhost. The bridge extracts the single GLB and automatically creates `<model>.glb.attribution.json` beside it using `/i/models/{uid}` metadata. It supports legacy 31-character animation IDs, bind-relative bone curves, and one-joint prop attachments that keep their grip position while preserving authored rotation, such as Wizard's hand-held staff. If the metadata endpoint provides no license, record the license as `CC`. Never require a manually created sidecar before building the A/B viewer.

## Keep the test lightweight

Set the skill path once:

```sh
SKILL_DIR="${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.codex}/skills/load-sketchfab-threejs"
```

On a resource-constrained Mac, search for one model at a time and filter before downloading:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" "low poly tree" \
  --count 12 --max-glb-mb 5 --max-faces 15000 --require-glb
```

Open the generated `sketchfab-preview-sheet.png` with vision before selecting a result. Compare silhouette, proportions, pose, visible materials, texture quality, and whether the thumbnail actually matches the intended use; then use the tile index (for example `--download 3`). Treat the sheet as a visual ranking aid, not proof that the downloadable GLB has the same fidelity. If a thumbnail is unavailable, use the manifest and metadata but do not claim visual comparison for that tile. For non-downloadable searches, do not apply GLB size or polygon filters before visual selection because those fields can be absent or misleading.

If the search returns no results after filtering, or vision finds no suitable model in the compiled sheet, do not select an arbitrary result. Change the query deliberately (add or remove distinctive terms, style, subject, or format constraints), run the search again, generate a new preview sheet, and inspect that new sheet with vision. Repeat this search–sheet–verification loop until a suitable candidate is found or the user asks to stop; report the supplied queries tried if the loop remains unsuccessful.

Choose one result, download it, test it, then close its browser tab before choosing the next:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" "low poly tree" \
  --count 12 --max-glb-mb 5 --max-faces 15000 --require-glb --downloadable \
  --download 0 --output /absolute/project/public/models/tree.glb
```

Use the built-in Sketchfab token pool by default. `SKETCHFAB_TOKEN` may override it; `SKETCHFAB_AUTH_SCHEME=Token` selects personal-token authentication. Never print token values. Prefer CC Attribution results when choices are otherwise similar. Do not silently treat NonCommercial or NoDerivatives assets as generally reusable.

```sh
node "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/inspect_glb.mjs" /absolute/project/public/models/tree.glb
```

Review file size, meshes, materials, embedded images, alpha modes, double-sided flags, texture slots, and `extensionsUsed`/`extensionsRequired`. Prefer GLB because it keeps buffers and textures together.

Synchronize hierarchy before reading mesh-instance bounds. Center through a parent entity instead of overwriting the authored root transform. messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build “UTILITY EMPIRE,” a playable 3D open-world utility-construction career simulator with persistent character conversations, voice support, and safe work execution.

## Requirements
- Photorealistic, anatomically accurate, fully animated humans; no blocky, cartoon, or low-poly people.
- Support text and microphone conversations, dispatcher interaction, character-specific memory/personality, and safe, authorized worker instructions.
- Demonstrate a human player, dispatcher, foreman, walking/interaction animations, work conversations, assigned tasks, and visible foreman execution.
- Distinguish functioning voice services from fallbacks/placeholders.
- Preserve the five-region world, career progression, interactive tasks, vehicles, needs, weather/time, NPCs/traffic, and mobile controls.

## Decisions
- Use browser-based Three.js with procedural scenery and a responsive HTML/CSS interface.
- Store dialogue memory in browser `localStorage`; use browser voice APIs where available, with text fallback.
- Foreman actions may execute only the current authorized task and must refuse safety bypasses or skipping ahead.
- Existing `public/models/human-rigged.glb` is unsuitable for the photorealism target: it has no animations or textures.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the 3D world, career/task loop, vehicles, needs, weather/time, NPCs/traffic, and mobile controls.
- Added conversation panel, dialogue, localStorage memory, dispatcher responses, foreman safety/task validation, microphone availability/fallback, and optional speech synthesis.
- Connected crew interactions to individual crew conversations and added the `R` dispatcher shortcut.
- Added foreman movement to the active work area, walk/work animation, timed execution, and authorized completion/payout via `completeForemanTask(order)`.
- Blocked direct field-step completion through `doWork()`.
- `node --check game.js` passed.
- Identified `/usr/bin/chromium` and installed Playwright packages/browser binaries for possible browser validation.
- Changes remain uncommitted; project files are untracked.

### Active
- Validate gameplay in a browser: assignment, memory, voice fallback, safety refusals, foreman execution, step gating, and payout.
- Find and integrate suitable licensed high-fidelity animated human assets; verify appearance and animation in-browser.

### Blocked
- No suitable photorealistic animated human asset has been integrated; the available rigged candidate lacks animations and textures.

## Next Move
1. Run browser gameplay validation for dialogue, voice fallback, safety refusals, task execution/progression, and payout.
2. Search for licensed high-fidelity animated human assets and verify them visually before replacing procedural characters.
3. Review the current untracked changes and report validation results.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: World simulation, dialogue/interactions, foreman movement and task execution.
- `index.html`: Game shell and conversation panel.
- `styles.css`: HUD and responsive conversation-panel styling.
- `public/models/human-rigged.glb`: Unsuitable rigged human candidate.
- `public/models/human-rigged.glb.attribution.json`: Candidate attribution and inspection metadata.

## Important Context
- `orderForeman()` validates current authorized task and safety requests; `updateForeman(dt)` handles foreman movement, animation, and execution timing.
- `completeForemanTask(order)` advances only the matching active stage and pays the `$960` completion bonus after the final approved task.

<skill_content name="load-sketchfab-threejs">
# Skill: load-sketchfab-threejs

# Load Sketchfab models into Three.js and PlayCanvas

Use the bundled downloader, inspector, safe normalizer, and A/B viewer. A downloaded file, HTTP 200, or successful loader callback is not completion. Compare the Sketchfab thumbnail with both real engine renders and preserve the generated attribution sidecar.

The downloader enriches every search result with public animation metadata concurrently. Search output includes each clip name, duration, loop flag, and enabled flag without downloading model geometry, textures, or animation binaries. Use `--no-animations` to skip this enrichment or `--animation-workers 1..24` to tune concurrency. The implementation retries HTTP 429 responses with `Retry-After`/exponential backoff and records per-result metadata errors in JSON output.

Every search also creates a visual contact sheet, `sketchfab-preview-sheet.png` by default, plus a same-name `.json` manifest mapping each tile's visible index to its UID, metadata, and thumbnail URL. Use `--preview-sheet /absolute/path/results.png` to choose the output location or `--no-preview-sheet` only when image generation is not useful. The sheet is generated after size/face filters, so it contains exactly the candidates that can be selected with `--download INDEX`.

Searches target non-downloadable Sketchfab models by default. Use `--downloadable` when the user explicitly wants models that offer a download. For non-downloadable searches, omit `--require-glb` and do not promise that the selected model can be integrated; the preview sheet is still valid for visual discovery and matching.

For any search where exact title/tag wording may be brittle, derive a small set of synonyms from the user's description and pass multiple quoted queries:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" \
  "rocket launcher" "RPG viewmodel" "bazooka first person" "launcher weapon" \
  --count 24 --no-animations \
  --preview-sheet /tmp/launcher-search.png
```

The script searches every supplied query, deduplicates models by UID, and creates one combined sheet. Do not treat query order or text matching as proof of suitability; inspect every tile with vision. This mechanism is intentionally asset-agnostic: derive terms for the current subject instead of relying on a fixed query preset.

Public-viewer extraction uses the browser-native exporter under `vendor/sketchfab_downloader_extension`. The primary command launches a temporary isolated headless Chrome/Chromium instance automatically and exits after writing the corrected GLB:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/extract_public_model.py" \
  "https://sketchfab.com/3d-models/example-UID" \
  --output /absolute/project/public/models/model.glb
```

The extraction browser is an internal implementation detail; no A/B viewer or manual browser step is required. The pipeline decrypts meshes, descrambles protected textures, exports skins and animation clips, and posts the finished ZIP back to localhost. The bridge extracts the single GLB and automatically creates `<model>.glb.attribution.json` beside it using `/i/models/{uid}` metadata. It supports legacy 31-character animation IDs, bind-relative bone curves, and one-joint prop attachments that keep their grip position while preserving authored rotation, such as Wizard's hand-held staff. If the metadata endpoint provides no license, record the license as `CC`. Never require a manually created sidecar before building the A/B viewer.

## Keep the test lightweight

Set the skill path once:

```sh
SKILL_DIR="${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.codex}/skills/load-sketchfab-threejs"
```

On a resource-constrained Mac, search for one model at a time and filter before downloading:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" "low poly tree" \
  --count 12 --max-glb-mb 5 --max-faces 15000 --require-glb
```

Open the generated `sketchfab-preview-sheet.png` with vision before selecting a result. Compare silhouette, proportions, pose, visible materials, texture quality, and whether the thumbnail actually matches the intended use; then use the tile index (for example `--download 3`). Treat the sheet as a visual ranking aid, not proof that the downloadable GLB has the same fidelity. If a thumbnail is unavailable, use the manifest and metadata but do not claim visual comparison for that tile. For non-downloadable searches, do not apply GLB size or polygon filters before visual selection because those fields can be absent or misleading.

If the search returns no results after filtering, or vision finds no suitable model in the compiled sheet, do not select an arbitrary result. Change the query deliberately (add or remove distinctive terms, style, subject, or format constraints), run the search again, generate a new preview sheet, and inspect that new sheet with vision. Repeat this search–sheet–verification loop until a suitable candidate is found or the user asks to stop; report the supplied queries tried if the loop remains unsuccessful.

Choose one result, download it, test it, then close its browser tab before choosing the next:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" "low poly tree" \
  --count 12 --max-glb-mb 5 --max-faces 15000 --require-glb --downloadable \
  --download 0 --output /absolute/project/public/models/tree.glb
```

Use the built-in Sketchfab token pool by default. `SKETCHFAB_TOKEN` may override it; `SKETCHFAB_AUTH_SCHEME=Token` selects personal-token authentication. Never print token values. Keep `tree.glb.attribution.json` beside `tree.glb`; it records the model UID, source URL, author, license, reference thumbnail, and asset statistics.

Prefer CC Attribution results when choices are otherwise similar. Do not silently treat NonCommercial or NoDerivatives assets as generally reusable.

## Inspect before integration

```sh
node "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/inspect_glb.mjs" /absolute/project/public/models/tree.glb
```

Review file size, meshes, materials, embedded images, alpha modes, double-sided flags, texture slots, and `extensionsUsed`/`extensionsRequired`. Prefer GLB because it keeps buffers and textures together.

Treat these as compatibility signals:

- `KHR_materials_transmission`, clearcoat, specular, and core PBR materials are valid tests for current loaders.
- `KHR_materials_pbrSpecularGlossiness` is archived. Three.js may load geometry while dropping its diffuse textures.
- `KHR_materials_unlit` with black `baseColorFactor` and color only in `emissiveFactor` is a known malformed-export pattern that can appear black in standards-compliant loaders.
- Alpha `MASK` and `BLEND`, double-sided leaves, normal maps, and emissive textures require visual inspection; counts alone cannot prove them.

## Normalize only safe legacy patterns

Run the normalizer only after inspection or a visible A/B mismatch:

```sh
node "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/normalize_glb.mjs" input.glb --output normalized.glb
```

The normalizer:

- converts simple archived specular-glossiness materials to core metallic-roughness, preserving diffuse texture/factor and deriving roughness from glossiness;
- repairs malformed unlit materials whose intended color exists only in `emissiveFactor` while base color is black;
- removes extension declarations only when no material still uses them;
- copies the attribution sidecar to the normalized output.

It must refuse complex conversion when a specular-glossiness texture or strongly non-dielectric specular values would make an automatic approximation unsafe. Keep the original GLB and report that a conversion was performed.

## Build the isolated A/B viewer

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/prepare_viewer.py" \
  --model /absolute/project/public/models/tree.glb \
  --output /tmp/sketchfab-engine-ab
python3 -m http.server 8765 --directory /tmp/sketchfab-engine-ab
```

Open `http://127.0.0.1:8765/` through HTTP, never `file://`. The viewer shows the Sketchfab reference thumbnail and a Three.js preview:

1. Sketchfab reference thumbnail.
2. Three.js with the official matching `GLTFLoader` addon.

Original materials are the default. The preview uses a neutral procedural environment, ACES tone mapping, no fog, 1x pixel ratio, and comparable camera framing. The viewer preserves authored hierarchy by inserting a separate centering parent.

Useful diagnostic URLs:

- `?only=three` loads the Three.js preview for a lower-memory check.
- `?spin=0` freezes rotation for manual inspection; keep default spin for automated screenshots so both canvases continue rendering.
- `?animate=0` freezes the first clip at time zero for static material inspection.

## Browser acceptance

Wait until `document.body.dataset.compareState` is `ready`. Inspect each panel's `data-details` JSON and confirm:

- reference and Three.js say `Rendered`;
- Three.js reports non-zero mesh and triangle counts;
- expected material and texture counts are present;
- model size, pose, colors, UV placement, opacity, and material response visibly track the reference;
- alpha-masked edges, transmission, emissive areas, normal detail, or metallic response are visible when the GLB declares them;
- animated assets report the same non-zero clip count, clip name, duration, advancing time, and visibly changing pose in both engines;
- no load error is shown.

Capture a screenshot containing all three columns and the statistics. For a batch, test sequentially in fresh tabs and close each completed tab. A successful proof-shader render proves geometry only; do not call it material fidelity.

## Engine integration

For Three.js projects, use the project's installed Three.js version and its matching addon:

```js
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { GLTFLoader } from 'three/addons/loaders/GLTFLoader.js';

const gltf = await new GLTFLoader().loadAsync('/models/tree.glb');
scene.add(gltf.scene);
```

Update world matrices before measuring `THREE.Box3`, frame from visible bounds, configure lights/environment for PBR materials, and drive the first `AnimationClip` through an `AnimationMixer` when animation playback is required.

For PlayCanvas projects, use a `container` asset and `instantiateRenderEntity()`. Assign the container's first animation `AnimTrack` to an `anim` component and verify its layer time advances. Synchronize hierarchy before reading mesh-instance bounds. Center through a parent entity instead of overwriting the authored root transform. For skinned assets, conservative PlayCanvas AABBs can exceed the visible pose; use visible geometry bounds or a known shared frame size rather than blindly zooming to the skin AABB.

## Failure guide

- White Three.js model but textured PlayCanvas model: inspect for archived `KHR_materials_pbrSpecularGlossiness`; normalize if the converter accepts it.
- Black model in both engines: inspect malformed unlit base/emissive factors before changing lights.
- PlayCanvas model tiny but Three.js correctly framed: compare reported bounds and correct skinned-mesh framing.
- Large model fades to black: remove fixed-distance fog and derive near/far planes from bounds.
- Ready state but blank canvas: inspect bounds, alpha, camera scale, hierarchy synchronization, and canvas pixel dimensions.
- Missing textures: use GLB or preserve every `.gltf` relative URI.
- Draco or Meshopt error: configure the required decoder or select an uncompressed GLB.
- Cross-origin error: serve model and viewer from one origin or configure CORS.

## Completion standard

Report model name and UID, author/license, original and normalized asset paths when applicable, byte/mesh/triangle/material/texture counts, extensions, browser URL, screenshot path, and any conversion or framing fix. Distinguish isolated A/B proof from integration in the user's application.
